more.good_when: A maintainer who restructures invoicer/sheet.py sees a test fail for each behavior of it that they break. Today the 78 tests all still pass when any of these behaviors is changed: a Description cell of two lines read as one line joined by a space (sheet.py:146); a negative number typed into a text-formatted Price cell, such as "-12.50", refused with how to make it a number (sheet.py:28); a number with spaces around it in a text-formatted cell refused the same way (sheet.py:232); a Quantity cell formatted as currency or percent refused as not a whole number (sheet.py:220); a Price cell formatted as percent refused as not a number (sheet.py:24); the column named by its two letters past Z, such as AA, in a refusal (sheet.py:245-252); and a path that exists but can't be opened, such as a folder or a file without read permission, refused with its reason (sheet.py:101-104). Each of these is what accounting meets in a refusal or an invoice, so a maintainer can change the structure there without fear only once a test shows it holds.
